eligibility.evidence: Overview and Exp. 1-2 (pp.8-23): GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 administered the property-induction phenomena of Osherson et al. 1990 and compared with new MTurk data (110 and 610 participants); sign tests and Spearman correlations reported.

A.title: Inductive reasoning in humans and large language models

paradigms.name: Property induction, forced choice of the stronger of two arguments (11 Osherson et al. phenomena x Mammals/Birds/Vehicles)
paradigms.source_paper: Osherson, Smith, Wilkie, Lopez & Shafir 1990; Rips 1975
paradigms.location: Experiment 1, pp.8-16, Table 1, Table 4; contamination discussion p.30

paradigms.name: Property induction, strength rating of individual one- and two-premise arguments
Similarity ratings of category pairs (0-20), compared with human similarity norms
paradigms.source_paper: De Deyne et al. 2008 (Leuven Natural Concepts Dataset)
paradigms.location: Extracting similarity judgments and Representation, pp.20-25, Figure 6

D.population: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers pre-screened for English: Exp. 1 N=110 analysed (120 recruited), Exp. 2 N=610, plus 40 for an Osherson replication; similarity norms from De Deyne et al. 2008
D.metric: sign test on which argument was rated stronger (Exp. 1); Spearman rho between model and human argument rankings, split-half reliability (Exp. 2)

E.headline: GPT-4 qualitatively matches humans on property induction apart from premise non-monotonicity; GPT-3.5 struggles to capture many aspects of human behaviour.

G.notes: Eleven phenomena pooled into one paradigm; E rows use the first-reported condition, so they understate the GPT-4 Non-Monotonicity failure. Prompt-variant results (S/C/A/Q/O) are not reported, only the best prompt. No query dates. Temperature 1 mentioned informally, results not shown. Human Diversity effect not replicated.
